content: Phenobarbital is a potent inducer of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which plays a critical role in the metabolism of numerous drugs. Co-administration of phenobarbital with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 can lead to significant reductions in plasma levels and therapeutic effects of these drugs. For example: 1. Sildenafil: Phenobarbital decreases sildenafil plasma levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs or avoidance of co-administration is recommended. 2. Silodosin: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of silodosin by accelerating its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Simvastatin: Phenobarbital decreases simvastatin levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or consider alternative therapy. 4. Siponimod: Co-administration with phenobarbital is not recommended, especially in patients with CYP2C9 1/3 or 2/3 genotypes, as it significantly reduces siponimod levels. 5. Sirolimus: Phenobarbital reduces sirolimus levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Sofosbuvir: Phenobarbital decreases sofosbuvir levels and its active metabolite (GS-331007) by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. This reduces its pharmacologic effect. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Velpatasvir: Phenobarbital reduces velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4 enzymes, as well as P-gp transporters. This may lead to reduced therapeutic efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Sonidegib: Phenobarbital decreases sonidegib levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 9. Sorafenib: Phenobarbital reduces sorafenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Sotagliflozin: Phenobarbital decreases sotagliflozin levels by inducing UGT1A9 glucuronidation, its major metabolic pathway. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Sotorasib: Phenobarbital reduces sotorasib levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Sparsentan: Phenobarbital decreases sparsentan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Stiripentol: Phenobarbital reduces stiripentol levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs increase sedation when used together. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Sufentanil: Co-administration with phenobarbital may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, hypotension, coma, or death due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use only when no alternatives exist, and monitor closely. 15. Tamsulosin: Phenobarbital decreases tamsulosin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Tazemetostat: Phenobarbital reduces tazemetostat levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Tetracycline: Phenobarbital decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Tezacaftor: Phenobarbital reduces tezacaftor levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Tivozanib: Phenobarbital decreases tivozanib levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Tizanidine: Phenobarbital reduces tizanidine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Tolvaptan: Phenobarbital decreases tolvaptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Tovorafenib: Phenobarbital reduces tovorafenib levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducers. 23. Trabectedin: Phenobarbital decreases trabectedin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Tucatinib: Phenobarbital reduces tucatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Ubrogepant: Phenobarbital decreases ubrogepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Ulipristal: Phenobarbital reduces ulipristal levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Upadacitinib: Phenobarbital decreases upadacitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 28. Abiraterone: Phenobarbital reduces abiraterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, increase abiraterone dosage frequency and monitor closely. 29. Acebutolol: Phenobarbital decreases acebutolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. 30. Amlodipine: Phenobarbital reduces amlodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 31. Amiodarone: Phenobarbital decreases amiodarone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Amitriptyline: Phenobarbital reduces amitriptyline levels by inducing CYP2C19, CYP3A4, and P-gp metabolism. Monitor closely. 33. Atorvastatin: Phenobarbital decreases atorvastatin levels by inducing CYP3A4 and P-gp metabolism. Monitor closely. 34. Avanafil: Phenobarbital reduces avanafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor erectile dysfunction treatment response carefully. 35. Belumosudil: Phenobarbital reduces belumosudil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase belumosudil dosage when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 36. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Phenobarbital reduces levels of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 and P-gp metabolism. This may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Monitor closely. 37. Bendamustine: Phenobarbital decreases bendamustine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor closely for changes in active metabolite concentrations. 38. Benperidol: Phenobarbital increases sedation when co-administered with benperidol. Monitor closely. 39. Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Phenobarbital reduces levels of this combination by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 40. Artesunate: Phenobarbital reduces artesunate levels by inducing UGT metabolism, decreasing the active metabolite DHA. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 41. Atenolol: Phenobarbital decreases atenolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. 42. Atogepant: Phenobarbital reduces atogepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust dosage to 30 mg or 60 mg daily when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 43. Azela
